verdicts.name: Coeliac disease
verdicts.reason: HLA DR3-DQ2.5 haplotype tag · Coeliac disease is essentially excluded: over 99 % of people with it carry one of these two haplotypes.

verdicts.name: Type 2 diabetes
verdicts.reason: TCF7L2 · One TCF7L2 T allele raises type 2 diabetes risk about 1.4-fold (A).

verdicts.name: Insulin resistance
verdicts.reason: FTO · Two FTO A alleles double that nudge (B).

verdicts.name: Atherosclerotic risk
verdicts.reason: APOE · no rule for Atherosclerotic risk fired on this call (e2/e3).

verdicts.name: High lipoprotein(a)
verdicts.reason: LPA · no rule for High lipoprotein(a) fired on this call (non-carrier).

verdicts.reason: HFE · no rule for Haemochromatosis fired on this call (no C282Y or H63D).

verdicts.reason: HLA DR3-DQ2.5 haplotype tag · no rule for Autoimmune thyroiditis (Hashimoto's) fired on this call (no DQ2.5 or DQ8 tag).

verdicts.reason: HLA DR3-DQ2.5 haplotype tag · no rule for Atrophic gastritis fired on this call (no DQ2.5 or DQ8 tag).

genes.verdict: e2/e3: ε2 lowers LDL and lowers dementia risk, and in rare cases carries type III hyperlipoproteinaemia.
genes.source: Bennet 2007 JAMA (APOE genotype and coronary risk, 82 studies); Farrer 1997 JAMA (APOE and Alzheimer meta-analysis); ClinVar rs429358 / rs7412.
Clarke 2009 N Engl J Med (PROCARDIS: rs10455872 and rs3798220 with Lp(a) and coronary disease); Kamstrup 2009 JAMA.

genes.verdict: Neither common HFE variant, so the usual genetic cause of iron overload is off the table.
genes.source: Feder 1996 Nat Genet (HFE discovery); EASL 2022 clinical practice guidelines on haemochromatosis; ClinVar rs1800562 (C282Y), rs1799945 (H63D).

genes.verdict: Coeliac disease is essentially excluded: over 99 % of people with it carry one of these two haplotypes.
genes.source: Monsuur 2008 PLoS ONE (the rs2187668 T allele tags DQ2.5-DR3, rs7454108 C tags DQ8); Karell 2003 Hum Immunol; NICE NG20 coeliac guidance on HLA testing as a rule-out; Zeitlin 2008 Clin Endocrinol and Jacobson 2008 Clin Immunol for DR3/DR4 and autoimmunity; rs660895 tags DRB1*04:01 (Raychaudhuri 2012 Nat Genet).

genes.verdict: 1 risk allele: about 40 % above the background risk, and the DPP trial showed lifestyle change erases most of it.
genes.source: Grant 2006 Nat Genet (deCODE, TCF7L2 and type 2 diabetes); Florez 2006 N Engl J Med (DPP: the risk is preventable by lifestyle).

genes.verdict: One copy, essentially no effect on homocysteine at normal folate intake.
genes.source: Frosst 1995 Nat Genet (C677T); Clarke 2012 PLoS Med (MTHFR, homocysteine and disease: the effect is small and folate-dependent); ACMG 2013 statement against routine MTHFR testing.

genes.verdict: Caffeine clears quickly; a morning coffee moves a draw much less.
genes.source: Cornelis 2006 JAMA (CYP1A2 genotype, coffee and myocardial infarction); PharmGKB rs762551 caffeine annotation.
Enattah 2002 Nat Genet (MCM6 rs4988235 and lactase persistence); Storhaug 2017 Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol (global prevalence).

genes.verdict: 2 risk alleles: roughly 2.4 kg more body weight on average, through appetite.
genes.source: Frayling 2007 Science (FTO and BMI); Kilpeläinen 2011 PLoS Med (physical activity attenuates the FTO effect by about 30 %).

genes.verdict: The common allele; the usual haemolysis triggers are safe on this account.
genes.source: Luzzatto 2020 Blood (G6PD deficiency); ClinVar rs1050828 (Val68Met, the A− allele); WHO G6PD classification.

genes.verdict: The usual transporter; no statin dose change on genetic grounds.
genes.source: SEARCH Collaborative Group 2008 N Engl J Med (SLCO1B1 variants and statin-induced myopathy); CPIC 2022 guideline for statins and SLCO1B1.
